---
title: "Numerical and graphical techniques"
subtitle: "Otto & Day, chapter 4, with PracticalCAS"
engine: julia
---

Before analysing a model, get a feel for it: iterate it, plot it against time,
cobweb it, and look at its phase plane. `simulate`, `cobweb` and
`bifurcation_data` return plain arrays, ready for any plotting package (with
PracticalBayesPlot loaded, `phaseplot` draws phase portraits directly).

```{julia}
using PracticalCAS
@syms n::nonneg r::positive K::positive
```

## Iterating a recurrence

The discrete logistic model `n(t+1) = n + r n (1 - n/K)` approaches `K`
smoothly for small `r`, oscillates for `1 < r < 2`, and cycles or behaves
chaotically beyond.

```{julia}
dl = recurrence(n => n + r * n * (1 - n / K))
for rv in (0.5, 1.8, 2.2, 2.8)
    u = simulate(dl, 0.1, 60; parameters = Dict(r => rv, K => 1)).u[:, 1]
    println("r = $rv: ", round.(u[end-3:end]; digits = 3))
end
```

```{julia}
#| include: false
u = simulate(dl, 0.1, 200; parameters = Dict(r => 0.5, K => 1)).u[:, 1]
@assert abs(u[end] - 1) < 1e-8
u = simulate(dl, 0.1, 400; parameters = Dict(r => 2.2, K => 1)).u[:, 1]
@assert abs(u[end] - u[end-2]) < 1e-8 && abs(u[end] - u[end-1]) > 0.1    # a 2-cycle
```

## Cobwebs

A cobweb diagram follows `n(t) → n(t+1)` on the plot of the map against the
diagonal. Its vertices:

```{julia}
cobweb(dl, 0.1, 3; parameters = Dict(r => 1.8, K => 1))
```

```{julia}
#| include: false
cw = cobweb(dl, 0.1, 3; parameters = Dict(r => 1.8, K => 1))
@assert size(cw) == (7, 2) && cw[1, :] == [0.1, 0.0] && cw[3, 1] == cw[3, 2]
```

## Bifurcation diagram

The long-run states as `r` varies show the period-doubling route to chaos.
Counting the distinct states at a few values:

```{julia}
bd = bifurcation_data(dl, r, [1.5, 2.2, 2.5, 2.7]; ic = 0.1, parameters = Dict(K => 1), keep = 64)
for rv in (1.5, 2.2, 2.5, 2.7)
    states = bd.state[bd.parameter .== rv]
    println("r = $rv: ", length(unique(round.(states; digits = 6))), " distinct states")
end
```

```{julia}
#| include: false
cnt(rv) = length(unique(round.(bd.state[bd.parameter .== rv]; digits = 6)))
@assert cnt(1.5) == 1 && cnt(2.2) == 2 && cnt(2.5) == 4 && cnt(2.7) > 8
```

The analysis in chapters 5 and 11 explains these numbers: `K` is stable for
`r < 2` and the 2-cycle for `2 < r < √6`.

```{julia}
stability(dl, Dict(n => K)).condition
```

```{julia}
#| include: false
@assert isequiv(stability(dl, Dict(n => K)).condition, r < 2)
```

## Solving an ODE numerically

The numerical solution of the logistic ODE agrees with the exact one:

```{julia}
@syms t::nonneg n₀::positive
lg = ode(n => r * n * (1 - n / K))
sol = simulate(lg, 0.1, 10; parameters = Dict(r => 1, K => 1))
exact = subs(dsolve(lg, t; ic = n₀), r => 1, K => 1, n₀ => 0.1)
maximum(abs(sol.u[i, 1] - evalf(exact, t => sol.t[i])) for i in eachindex(sol.t))
```

```{julia}
#| include: false
@assert maximum(abs(sol.u[i, 1] - evalf(exact, t => sol.t[i])) for i in eachindex(sol.t)) < 1e-7
```

## Phase plane: nullclines and trajectories

For Lotka–Volterra competition the nullclines are lines; where they cross is
the coexistence equilibrium, and trajectories go there when each species
limits itself more than the other.

```{julia}
@syms n₁::nonneg n₂::nonneg α::positive β::positive
comp = ode(n₁ => n₁ * (1 - n₁ - α * n₂), n₂ => n₂ * (1 - n₂ - β * n₁))
nullclines(comp, 1, n₂), nullclines(comp, 2, n₂)
```

```{julia}
traj = simulate(comp, [0.05, 0.9], 60; parameters = Dict(α => 0.5, β => 0.5))
traj.u[end, :]
```

```{julia}
#| include: false
@assert all(abs.(traj.u[end, :] .- 2 / 3) .< 1e-6)      # (1 - α)/(1 - αβ)
@assert any(isequiv(c, (1 - n₁) / α) for c in nullclines(comp, 1, n₂))
```
